A Leading Co-Educational Independent School in West Sussex
A Leading Co-Educational Independent School in West Sussex
Discover Great Ballard, an independent school near Chichester, inspiring children from nursery through to GCSE.
A Great Independent Education from Nursery to 16
At Great Ballard, we aspire to greatness. It's in our name, but also in our heritage. Set in the beautiful West Sussex countryside, within the South Down National Park, the great outdoors is matched by a warm, caring and nurturing environment indoors. Filled with great leaders, great thinkers, great carers and great motivators. Special people who encourage self-discovery and expression in all our pupils. Encouraging them to progress from great smilers, great tidy uppers, inquisitive great explorers, confident great performers, great doers and great learners to become positively great self-believers, great achievers and great role models.
Discover Great Ballard School
Welcome from the Head
When Ivor Poole established Great Ballard in 1924 he made a promise that the school would be different. That courage to stand out from the crowd still energises us a century later. Poole wanted everyone to be cared for and treated fairly and Great Ballard today is a family in which everyone matters and no one is invisible. It is a school that cares, a school built completely around its pupils, a school with a heart.Poole’s principles remain unchanged but the world beyond school refuses to stand still. Our duty to equip young people for an unpredictable future has never been more apparent. Our curriculum is broad and forward thinking and we encourage pupils to look beyond our idyllic West Sussex setting and develop the skills required to be adaptable and to make a difference in their world. We focus on leadership, problem solving and enterprise while covering a broad range of traditional subjects. We also nurture a passion for technology, computer science and communication skills which we champion along with the highest standards of literacy and numeracy. We see unique potential in all our children and support them to become the very best versions of themselves.With an ethos rooted in building the strongest relationships and on empathy and respect, our young people recognise a need to be role models and to lift others. We take education beyond the classroom, making the most of our wonderful location to prioritise creativity, teamwork and pupil well-being. And we never lose sight of the value of the arts and exercise in shaping happy, healthy and resilient young lives. Great journeys begin with great preparation.Matt King, Head

Superb Science Fair!
On Friday 15th May, we welcomed Year 5 and 6 pupils from local West Sussex schools to showcase their amazing research projects. There was some incredible work on display from the young scientists who had investigated everything from mould to parachutes and from batteries to tastebuds! The judges were impressed by the quality of their work and the confidence with which they were able to explain what they had discovered. Huge congratulations to everyone who took part and to the overall winners from Great Ballard and Oakwood School.

From Aspiration to Achievement
Set in the beautiful West Sussex countryside near Chichester, Great Ballard is an inspirational setting for the next stage of your child's education. We are passionate about finding opportunities for all pupils to build their self-confidence, to challenge themselves and to find areas in which they can excel. These are crucial years, where our key aim is to keep our eye on the future and on the skills young people really need to be a success, both in exams and in the wider world. Our small class sizes, academic monitoring, outstanding pastoral care and forward-thinking curriculum ensure our students have the best foundations to flourish.
Academic Excellence from Year 7 to GCSE
Our aim is always to be inclusive and to tailor our approach to meet our students' needs. Education is about opening doors and each student's ambition becomes our goal. Small classes, quality teaching and high expectations form the backbone of our academic success.
Aspire
Years 7 and 8
Years 7 and 8 are based in the senior part of the school but retain their own character and Prep School ethos. Our specialist teachers ensure high academic aspirations in the classroom as students look towards their GCSE choices, but we also offer a full timetable of creative and physical subjects, maintaining an emphasis on community activities and personal wellbeing time to ensure the best outcomes for all.
Achieve
Years 9-11
In Years 9-11, the focus switches to preparation for GCSEs over three years, allowing enough time not only for the demanding new syllabuses, but also for the retention of curricular breadth and the holistic principles that underpin our 4H school. Year 9 will be focused more on the skills required at GCSE level rather than the specific curriculum content, ensuring that students who join us from local Prep Schools can adapt quickly. Those pupils will be able to choose their GCSE options before starting with us. Pupils also have the option to study for a project qualification to aid them in becoming inquisitive and independent learners.
A Forward-Thinking Senior School Curriculum
Our tailored and forward-thinking curriculum supports every student to achieve their best, while also introducing them to real world learning experiences and equipping them with the skills to flourish beyond Great Ballard.
Building Learning Power
As part of our unique curriculum, all senior students continue to benefit from timetabled lessons in computer skills and technology, learning how to utilise IT effectively in their studies and how to present their ideas. They also follow our Learning2Learn curriculum, with lessons that teach them how to motivate themselves and become independent learners. This tailored programme covers revision and homework strategies, how to extend learning and develop a growth mindset, as well as how to communicate ideas, how to initiate projects, how to collaborate and how to evaluate successes.
Leadership and Personal Development
Pupils are given opportunities to practise presentation and leadership skills both within school and in the wider community. Our Senior pupils are trained as peer mentors and are encouraged to be role models within our school, leading and organising assemblies, events and meetings. As they move up the school there are increasing opportunities for work experience and a programme of careers and future schools talks. From Year 9 onwards all students are given the opportunity to take part in the Duke of Edinburgh Award Scheme.
4H Skills and Diploma
Our Senior pupils are challenged to develop skills based on curiosity and problem solving; teamwork and communication; self-awareness, empathy and reflection; resilience and self-care. They work towards our Aspire Diploma, awarded at the end of Year 8 and our Achieve Diploma, awarded at the end of Year 11. They are encouraged to use these skills to tackle issues within the school and wider community and take part in a range of charity and entrepreneurial projects.
Activities, Careers and Life Skills
In the Senior School, pupils have time apportioned each week for activities that develop crucial life skills and contribute towards their 4H diploma. Alongside creative and practical activities, students will have the opportunity to do Duke of Edinburgh award, participate in an inspiring careers and enterprise programme and gain their extended project qualification (EPQ). They will continue to study communications and technology with the opportunity to gain Microsoft qualifications, and, right up until Year 11, every student will continue to have timetabled lessons in which they cook, grow and focus on wellbeing.
Wellbeing and Pastoral Care
We believe wellbeing is the foundation that allows the real learning to happen and Great Ballard has always been known for its outstanding pastoral care, built on positive relationships. All pupils have both a form tutor and a champion chosen by them, who remains a consistent source of support and encouragement. The wellbeing of every student in our school remains a priority throughout their time here. We have timetabled wellbeing sessions in which pupils are given support to understand and manage their emotions and relationships. Senior pupils are also trained in communication skills and as peer mentors to help them play a productive role in our community.
Sport, Fitness and Healthy Living
Senior School pupils continue to pursue excellence in both team and individual sports and they make use of the school pool and its idyllic 30 acre site. While the emphasis on competition is not lost, there is an increasing focus on the health benefits of sporting activity. It is our ambition that every student leaves Great Ballard enjoying sport and recognising the role that physical exercise can play in shaping healthy, happy lives. Students all have a personal fitness plan that encompasses mental and physical health and nurtures their well-being through a tailored approach. Some pupils will choose to study PE to GCSE level, but all will experience it as part of a curricular unit called MAP which includes cookery, nutrition and gardening.
“Every student has an individual fitness plan and leaves us understanding the role that sport plays in shaping healthy, happy lives.”
Supporting Every Student to Achieve Their Goals
Small class sizes, and engaged and empathetic staff, ensure we know every student and family well. Alongside ongoing teacher assessment, we use standardised testing to monitor each pupil's potential and progress, allowing us to understand their expected levels of achievement and to put support in place to ensure their best outcomes at GCSE.Students and parents receive attainment and effort grades every half term. As well as their actual attainment grade, students are given a challenge grade. Challenge grades show potential, based on nationally standardised data, and they encourage students to work towards aspirational yet achievable targets. Our excellent learning support department produces individual learning programmes and pupil passports to support those with learning needs, while our 'Go Beyond' scholarship programme provides stretch and a tailored programme for those identified as gifted and talented.
“Great Ballard pupils are confident, empathetic and motivated.”
The Great Ballard journey is all about preparation, for the next steps in school and ultimately for the world beyond. In Years 7&8 we encourage our students to aspire. The broad, outward facing senior curriculum helps them to better understand their world and equips them with the habits and skills to thrive within it. Our tailored approach for each student delivers the confidence they will need to turn aspiration into achievement as they progress through their three year GCSE course. And with each term closer to the end of their time at Great Ballard we increase the focus on life skills and leadership and the amount of careers advice we provide. We support them fully in taking their next step, helping them to find the very best schools and colleges to build on the successes they achieve with us. Students will leave on a variety of different journeys but all with the same confidence and ambition to live healthy, happy and purposeful lives.

pageCache.pageTitle: Between words and numbers, can technology help us turn the page?
pageCache.text:
Between words and numbers, can technology help us turn the page?
As Head of English, much of my working life is spent interpreting words and language. However, for the last 14 years, I have also held another job, one in which I (try to) interpret numbers, graphs, arrows and data every day.
Mr Duffield knows this is not because I secretly hope one day to add teaching Maths to my CV. Nor is it because I hope to become a data scientist. It is because I was diagnosed with Type 1 Diabetes in my early twenties. Unlike teaching, my position as a full-time working pancreas is not one from which I will ever be able to fully retire.
Research has previously suggested that a person with Type 1 Diabetes makes around 180 more health related decisions every day than someone without Diabetes. However, as technology and AI advance, the job description of a full-time working pancreas is gradually becoming a little less demanding.
This Summer, I moved to Dexcom’s G7 sensor, which communicates directly with my insulin pump. I still use an app on my phone to check my glucose levels and administer insulin for food, so I am by no means redundant as a pancreas just yet. However, my pump and sensor now communicate continually, using an algorithm to respond to changes in my glucose levels and automatically adjust my background insulin. Technology is beginning to make some of those decisions for me. As that technology continues to develop, it has the potential to give me back more time and attention. Ironically, those are the very two things we so often fear technology is taking away from us.
Also this Summer, I have spent much of my time surrounded by physical books, which is what one would imagine to be a Head of English’s dream. Mr Joseph has enjoyed observing the process and offering helpful commentary on my progress, noting that the books appear simply to have moved from one pile to another. Mrs King has provided much needed humour, particularly after Mrs Hardwick popped in and enthusiastically informed me that some of the bookshelves were, in fact, double sided. At that point, I realised I had even more books to sort through than I had first thought. Meanwhile, Kirsty has continued to respond extremely positively to every new ‘book list’ I have sent her, and there have been quite a few.
I am really thrilled about what the Library is becoming and what it can offer our students. It has also left me thinking about my ‘two’ jobs. In one, I am embracing technology and increasingly relying on what it can do for me. In the other, I spend much of my time championing books, reading and the value of the physical page.
In September, technology will also become part of our plans for developing reading across the school through the introduction of Accelerated Reader. This has made me think again about my message at the end of World Book Week, when I encouraged our school community to scroll less and read more. I still stand by it. Perhaps, though, the relationship between technology and reading does not need to be quite so binary. The question is less about whether we use technology and more about what we use it for. Accelerated Reader isn’t replacing the book. The reading still comes first, with the technology coming afterwards through quizzes and progress tracking, hopefully adding some motivation and allowing us to see and celebrate the reading that is already happening. We are also subscribing to the Collins Big Cat eLibrary, widening students’ access to stories, graphic novels and other reading material. It is another option and falls in line with the government’s Year of National Reading message.
Alongside this, I am particularly excited about the physical Library. At the beginning of September, we will officially open and launch the Library, and we are really looking forward to marking the occasion by welcoming award winning author Iqbal Hussain, whose novel The Night I Borrowed Time will be studied by our Year 6 students this year. It feels like a fitting way to begin this next chapter for our Library and, hopefully, for reading across the school.
We want the Library to become somewhere students enjoy spending time, whether they are browsing the shelves, discovering new authors and genres, talking about books or simply sitting and reading. I am looking forward to seeing what the students make of it.
Maybe that is where I have landed with my ‘two’ jobs. Technology doesn’t have to replace what we value about the physical experience. Sometimes, it can simply sit alongside it. Used in the right way, it might even give us more time, more access or another route to something we enjoy.
So, if I may, perhaps I will amend my World Book Week message slightly. Scroll less, read more, but use technology well. If technology can give me back some of the time and attention I currently spend being my own pancreas, I already know what I would like to do with it...

Great Beginnings with Seasons at Great Ballard
At Great Ballard, children from age 2 enjoy a nurturing start in the beautiful West Sussex countryside. Our cosy indoor space provides a safe and welcoming environment where every child can settle, explore, play and grow at their own pace, supported by their key person.
Discover a Child-Centred Curriculum Shaped Around Every Child
Seasons Nursery is nestled at the heart of Great Ballard School. For ten years, Seasons has delivered unique and innovative early years education through its sister setting Seasons at Aldingbourne, based at Aldingbourne Country Centre. At Seasons, we pride ourselves on our partnerships and our community. We thrive when collaborating with like-minded educators. That’s what makes Seasons at Great Ballard so exciting.
Not only do we deliver our own unique mix of quality education in a beautiful woodland setting, but as children grow, they have the option to continue their journey seamlessly through the school who shares the same vision…to deliver exceptional education which prioritises wellbeing and innovation and nurtures confidence, curiosity, invention and ambition.

Why Choose Great Ballard?
Our welcoming School Office team look after every aspect of the admissions process and should be the first port of call for all prospective parents. Our main entry points are at Reception, Year 3, Year 7 and Year 9 but, subject to us being able to match course requirements, students can join Great Ballard in West Sussex any time during the school year, even mid-term, as long as we have space. There is no ‘typical’ Great Ballard family. While some pupils join us from other independent schools, an equal amount are coming to independent education for the first time. Our ambition is always to be inclusive and to tailor our approach to meet our students’ needs.
Step 1: Arrange a Tour
The best way to get a feel for our school near Chichester would be to come and visit us. We always welcome prospective parents to our organised open morning events or you can arrange a 1:1 tour during school hours, to experience first-hand day-to-day life at Great Ballard.
Step 2: Register Your Interest
Following your visit, you will be able to register your child. You will need to complete our Registration Form and submit a £120 (non-refundable) registration fee. This registers your interest in a place for your child in their required year group, but does not guarantee them a place.Once both the registration form and associated payment have been received, your application will be processed.
Step 3: Taster days and Assessment
Taster sessions, the length and number of which will depend on your child’s age and what will make them feel most comfortable.Pre-Prep aged children (Reception to Year 2) will be invited to join us for “New Friends” days, during which your child would be informally assessed whilst experiencing a normal day with their peer group.Prep School and Senior children (Years 3-11) will be invited to join us for two taster days, the first being a normal day spent with their peer group and the second allowing us to carry out some standardised assessments in Maths, English, Verbal and Non-Verbal Reasoning.
Step 4: Offer and Admission
Your child will be offered a place on the basis of a successful taster session and/or assessments plus references and a copy of their latest report sought from their current school.Parents are asked to complete our Acceptance Form, which is based on our terms and conditions, in order to confirm the acceptance of a place.‍Parents are also asked to pay a £500 deposit to guarantee their child’s place. This deposit is refundable when your child leaves Great Ballard.Before your child joins Great Ballard, we will keep you updated with events and you will receive a joining pack and be invited to relevant information meetings.
*Please note that there will be a 30% reduction in fees for the Summer Term 2020 for current pupils due to the nationwide school closures as a result of COVID-19. We are also freezing our termly fees for the academic year 2020-2021 to help you through the economic crisis that COVID-19 has caused. The school has put in place a Distance Learning Provision consisting of a structured timetable involving Google Classroom, live teaching and other interactive online resources to ensure that the children's educational and mental health needs continue to be adequately met.

Curious Minds: Saturday Enrichment Sessions
Parent Partnership
At Great Ballard, we aim to create a family environment in everything we do. We welcome parents and grandparents and hope they will feel a part of our school in West Sussex. Whether it’s for formal parent evenings, joining a weekend Groundforce volunteering morning, spectating at matches and school plays or simply enjoying morning coffee on the terrace or in the library at one of our regular family events, we understand that the opportunity to feel part of the community and form friendships is important for the whole family.We are delighted to include parents in the event planning of the school and invite parents to join ‘Friends of Great Ballard’ (FoGB for short). The Friends volunteer as class reps to help welcome new families, keep their class updated with information and organise social events for children and parents. FoGB are responsible for putting on many of our marvellous annual events including the Christmas Fair and the Summer Fete. These events help to reinforce a sense of community that we consider paramount to our school and all money raised goes towards benefitting the school, such as funding new equipment and resources, as well as supporting local charities. Anyone is welcome to get involved and it is a fantastic way to get to know other parents. It doesn’t matter how much or how little time you have to offer, FoGB would be delighted to hear from you.
Grow with Us
It’s not just our pupils who grow at Great Ballard. We are always on the lookout for enthusiastic, forward thinking and purposeful people who are interested in becoming part of our journey and our ever strengthening team. From our classrooms to our kitchens and from our domestic staff to our office team you will find people who understand the school’s vision and are excited about delivering the very best outcomes for our children. If you are keen to be part of something great then take a look at our vacancies below or get in touch with Jacqui Whall at j.whall@greatballard.co.uk.

We will consider a job share for this role.

We Welcome the World Beyond Our School Grounds
Great Ballard is a tight-knit and happy community but we are always looking outwards and creating links with the world beyond our gates. We regularly open our doors to the public and the school is a venue for weddings, activity camps and sports clubs. We establish links with local businesses and support our village and our neighbours. But above all we teach our pupils the value of service, charity and giving. It matters to us that children set their own goals and plan their own fundraising projects. They learn life skills along the way, the power of purpose and the value of prioritising activism over apathy.

pageCache.text:
A welcome from the Heads of School
Hello everyone, we are looking forward to having everyone back for another wonderful year at Great Ballard! At Great Ballard, we want to help people to feel encouraged by others and to make them more confident, kind and ambitious. We hope to support you in trying new things, using the student voice and in looking after one another, all while having fun and achieving great things. In the past year, we have seen a great number of impressive achievements in academic work, in sports, in the arts and in all other areas, and we are certain that this year will be just as successful.
As Heads of School, we are also looking forward to making sure that the move into GCSE life is as smooth as possible. To this end, we would like to organise a session every term in which we can talk about our own experiences of GCSEs, answer any questions people may have, give some advice and be honest about what real life at GCSE level is like. We hope that these sessions will give us a useful chance to support and give help to everyone as they look to the next phase of their education.
We are proud to be with you and look forward to seeing the wonderful achievements you will make. Let’s make this year one in which you work hard, play hard, and most importantly, be kind.
We would also like to oversee the Student Council meetings, by attending and helping to guide meetings throughout the year, making sure that everyone has the opportunity to have their voices heard. We want to make sure that the Student Council continues to be an effective way for the students to contribute to and improve life at Great Ballard.
We look forward to seeing you all soon,
Theo Willson and Georgi Giles

A Leading Co-Educational Independent School in West Sussex
A Leading Co-Educational Independent School in West Sussex
Discover Great Ballard, an independent school near Chichester, inspiring children from nursery through to GCSE.
A Great Independent Education from Nursery to 16
At Great Ballard, we aspire to greatness. It's in our name, but also in our heritage. Set in the beautiful West Sussex countryside, within the South Down National Park, the great outdoors is matched by a warm, caring and nurturing environment indoors. Filled with great leaders, great thinkers, great carers and great motivators. Special people who encourage self-discovery and expression in all our pupils. Encouraging them to progress from great smilers, great tidy uppers, inquisitive great explorers, confident great performers, great doers and great learners to become positively great self-believers, great achievers and great role models.
Discover Great Ballard School
Welcome from the Head
When Ivor Poole established Great Ballard in 1924 he made a promise that the school would be different. That courage to stand out from the crowd still energises us a century later. Poole wanted everyone to be cared for and treated fairly and Great Ballard today is a family in which everyone matters and no one is invisible. It is a school that cares, a school built completely around its pupils, a school with a heart.Poole’s principles remain unchanged but the world beyond school refuses to stand still. Our duty to equip young people for an unpredictable future has never been more apparent. Our curriculum is broad and forward thinking and we encourage pupils to look beyond our idyllic West Sussex setting and develop the skills required to be adaptable and to make a difference in their world. We focus on leadership, problem solving and enterprise while covering a broad range of traditional subjects. We also nurture a passion for technology, computer science and communication skills which we champion along with the highest standards of literacy and numeracy. We see unique potential in all our children and support them to become the very best versions of themselves.With an ethos rooted in building the strongest relationships and on empathy and respect, our young people recognise a need to be role models and to lift others. We take education beyond the classroom, making the most of our wonderful location to prioritise creativity, teamwork and pupil well-being. And we never lose sight of the value of the arts and exercise in shaping happy, healthy and resilient young lives. Great journeys begin with great preparation.Matt King, Head

Set within 30 acres of the South Downs National Park and the Moore’s International Dark Sky Reserve, Great Ballard is ideally situated to provide a stunningly natural educational environment combined with excellent transport links across the county. It is located between the cathedral city of Chichester and the charming market towns of Arundel and Petworth, an area steeped in history and boasting easy access to sandy beaches, fishing villages, historical and family attractions; it is one of the most beautiful locations in South-East England. Although the school is nestled near the south coast, London Victoria is approximately a 75-minute ride away from Barnham or Chichester train stations, Gatwick and Heathrow are easily accessible and Great Ballard School is less than 30 miles from Brighton and Portsmouth.
South Downs National Park and Eartham Woods
Great Ballard Venue Hire
Nestled in the South Downs National Park, Eartham House is the perfect setting for away-days, events, family occasions, parties, group training, residential workshops and conferences, with plenty of free parking on site, impressive facilities and catering packages available to suit varied group sizes. For those looking to host training our large classroom spaces, set within the historic main building, are equipped with interactive whiteboards and wireless broadband.Easily accessible from the A27, you can be given exclusive usage during school holidays as well as plenty of other tailored options to ensure your event is hassle-free and creates a great impression for your clients and staff.
Facilities Hire
Our 30 acres of beautiful grounds are available for:– Sports training– Outdoor celebrations – we are also able to accommodate marquees– Children’s birthday partiesOur pitches, tennis courts, netball courts, cricket pitches and heated swimming pool are also available to hire by sports clubs and individuals.
Wedding Venue Hire
Eartham House has been a popular wedding reception venue for many years – some of the couples happily married at Eartham House have even returned with their children years later to attend the school! Set in 30 acres of glorious Sussex countryside, our beautiful grade II listed venue sets a stunning scene for weddings and special celebrations.Eartham House is situated in the quiet, unspoilt hamlet of Eartham and is exclusively yours with full use of the dining room, conservatory, reception halls, drawing room, adjoining dance and entertainment room, extensive gardens and ample free parking for your special day.We have a network of florists and photographers as well as an impressive catering team to help you plan your wedding day. Catering for all these events may be available on request. For more information, to arrange a visit or to check availability please contact our Business Manager on 01243 814236.
